Bash(python3 -m unittest -q; python3 -c 'from slugify import slugify as s; print([s(x…
Allow Bash(python3 -m unittest -q; python3 -c 'from slugify import slugify as s;
print([s(x) for x in ["--a--b--", "!!!", "", "Café au lait", "C++ & Rust"]])')?
Tests pass now, but accented letters get dropped ("Café" becomes "caf"). I'll handle
that too by converting accented letters to their plain ASCII versions first.
"""The part of a URL that names a page: "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world"."""
python3 -m unittest -q; python3 -c 'from slugify import slugify as s; print([s(x)
for x in ["Café au lait", "Ünïcödé Straße", "!!!", "C++ & Rust", "日本"]])')?
The slugify tests pass now (4 of 4, including one I added).
only replaced each space with a hyphen. Punctuation was kept (
), and spaces at the ends or in a row turned into extra hyphens (
: any run of characters that isn't a lowercase letter or digit
now becomes a single hyphen, and hyphens are trimmed from both ends.
accented letters were being dropped, so "Café" came out as "caf". They're
now converted to plain letters first, so "Café au lait" becomes
• Letters with no plain-letter equivalent are dropped: "Straße" becomes
• Titles with no Latin letters or digits, such as "日本" or "!!!", become an empty
If titles like these can come up, you'll need to decide what they should turn into,
such as a fallback slug or a transliteration library.
